These are prior-based estimates from general knowledge of NAS-Bench-201, not computed from the benchmark data.

The main heuristics I used:
- Edge 2 (1→2) being none: the cell's connectivity is reduced, so the remaining edges matter more. Adding a conv on edge 1 or 5 then has a larger positive effect.
- Edge 3 (0→3) as a skip_connect or conv already provides a direct path. Edits elsewhere then matter less.
- Interactions of consistent size across all three datasets are fairly rare, so N gets most of the mass.
